oncall-bot: PAGER: gpu-pool scalegrid-eu-1 queue growth detected, autoscaler health degraded. error rate rising. paging @Sam (oncall) and @Anika. https://infra.metrics/pools/scalegrid-eu-1 :rotating_light:
Sam (oncall): I'm awake, grabbing logs and metrics now. putting a short blameless note in incident channel.
Priya (ml-runtime): seeing sustained enqueue rate ~ 3.2k reqs/min over last 6m. queue length at pool-level: 14,200. autoscaler logs show repeated backoff and "max_scale_reached" messages.
Jorge (infra): checking provider quotas. our recent scale history shows attempts to add 16 GPUs but provider returned 429s/Throttled. provider account eu-1 has soft quota 200, current use 198.
Sam (oncall): ok — initial impact: some requests to /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings in EU are getting delayed >20s or 429s. Marta, any customer hits yet?
Marta (support): Twitter alert from customer acct 'shelf.ai' reporting spike in 429s and timeouts. I opened ticket #INC-4237. Early estimate: ~7% of production requests failing in eu region across several mid-size tenants.
Anika (sre-lead): plan: 1) triage autoscaler health and heartbeat, 2) short-term mitigation to reduce tail latency (route critical customers to fallback pool), 3) manual scale fallback if provider allows, 4) timeline and comms. Sam, take step 1+2. Priya, give fallback model options. Jorge, attempt manual quota bump.
Sam (oncall): running quick checks:
```
# check queue sizes
curl -s https://internal-metrics/api/pools/scalegrid-eu-1 | jq '.queue_size, .inflight, .pending'
# autoscaler logs
kubectl logs deploy/autoscaler-eu -n infra | tail -n 50
```
Autoscaler tail contains repeated lines: "scale attempt failed: provider throttle, will backoff" and "heartbeat missed: 3/3".
Priya (ml-runtime): fallback: we can route some routes to a smaller quantized model variant `rwd-quant-1.4b` with ~30% lower throughput cost and similar latency for short prompts. For embeddings we can switch to `embed-lite-2` which is slightly lower quality but mitigates failures. Can be toggled in routing layer via feature-flag.
Jorge (infra): I submitted quick quota request to cloud provider support, but wont be approved fast enough. I can spin up a temporary additional node group in eu with 8 gpus on our spare provider account if approved by finance. Need :thumbsup: from product or finance to proceed.
Ben (product): we should prioritize routing for paying customers first. Approve spinning temp group for critical tenants only. :+1:
Sam (oncall): starting immediate mitigations:
- Add routing rule: divert `org:high-commit` and `org:enterprise-*` to fallback pools (quantized variants)
- Enable aggressive KV/prefix caching for shared prompts to reduce repeated tokens
- Initiate capacity drain for scalegrid-eu-1 to prevent new long-running jobs from piling up (will still finish in-flight)
I will post commands when ready.
Priya (ml-runtime): routing toggles: pushing a canary change to routing service now. This will affect ~12% of current traffic and should cut effective queue growth rate by ~40%.
Sam (oncall): commands executed:
```
# add routing override
curl -X POST https://routing/api/overrides -d '{"target_orgs": ["enterprise-*","high-commit"], "model":"rwd-quant-1.4b"}'
# increase cache TTL for common prompts
kubectl patch configmap prompt-cache -n runtime --patch '{"data":{"ttl":"45s"}}'
```
Sam (oncall): immediate effect: queue growth rate dropped to ~1k req/min within 90s. error rate for routed customers decreased. still seeing elevated queue for low-priority queues.
Jorge (infra): manual node group spin-up started (account: spare-eu-ops). Estimated time to available ~6-8m. Creating 8 gpus.
Anika (sre-lead): good. parallel tasks: postmortem owner (Anika), SLAs/commms (Ben), customer comms draft (Marta). Sam keep triage updates every 5m.
Marta (support): drafting customer message to affected tenants: short note, root-cause pending, mitigation in progress, ETA ~15-20m for resolution for most tenants.
Priya (ml-runtime): note: some long-running jobs in queue are hogging KV cache and blocking efficient batching. Suggest a short eviction window for jobs >2m to favor throughput. Thoughts?
Anika (sre-lead): agree, but need to be careful with in-flight jobs. Sam, can you identify top offending job types?
Sam (oncall): running probe, top job types: large-dialogue-gen (30%), heavy-summarize (25%), embeddings-batch (20%), rest small. We can apply eviction to `heavy-summarize` and `embeddings-batch` for low-priority orgs.
Sam (oncall): applying eviction policy change now: `kubectl exec autoscaler -- /bin/sh -c "echo \"evict: {max_runtime:120, target_queues:[\"low-priority\"]}\" > /etc/autoscaler/policy"`
Sam (oncall): manual node group ready +8 gpus, attaching to cluster, autoscaler recognized new capacity. scalegrid-eu-1 available capacity rose from 2 to 10 gpus.
Sam (oncall): within 2m we see queue drop from 11.4k -> 2.1k, tail latency improving, 429s dropping to normal noise.
Marta (support): customers updated. 'shelf.ai' confirmed degraded but recovering, they report requests now processed.
Anika (sre-lead): current status: partial mitigations applied (routing fallback + temporary nodes + evictions). Impact window estimated 00:25 - 00:39 UTC. Need followups: full root cause and action items.
Priya (ml-runtime): immediate hypothesis: autoscaler misread heartbeat condition during sustained provider throttling -> backoff loop with inadequate fallback (no cross-pool failover) -> queues amplified by large-batch jobs that don't get batched across queues.
Jorge (infra): provider throttle + near-quota meant scale attempts queued at provider API level triggered exponential backoff in our autoscaler. Our autoscaler didn't fall back to 'fallback-node-pool' due to a gating check on pool labels. That gating check prevented quick failover.
Anika (sre-lead): action items (assignments inline):
- (Anika) Run full postmortem and timeline (doc link placeholder)
- (Priya) Add routing-first fallback in autoscaler: if provider throttle occurs X times within Y minutes, toggle route to fallback pools automatically.
- (Jorge) Remove strict label gating that blocks cross-pool failover and add test coverage.
- (Sam) Add runbook steps to manually spin and attach spare-account node groups faster (reduce manual time to 2m).
- (Marta) Post customer incident notes and update any affected SLA tickets.
- (Ben) Evaluate SLA weighting to ensure paying customers hit fallback earlier.
Anika (sre-lead): timeline notes for postmortem:
- 5409873210 first alert from pager
- 5409873250 autoscaler displayed repeated backoff logs
- 5409873300 routing canary pushed
- 5409873360 temp nodes requested
- 5409873420 eviction policy applied
- 5409873500 temp nodes attached and accepted by autoscaler
- 5409873585 queue largely drained, errors returned to baseline
- 5409873810 incident declared resolved for majority of customers (monitoring to continue)
Sam (oncall): logging this as RESOLVED for oncall. leaving follow-ups in the postmortem doc.
oncall-bot: Incident incident:5409873210 status changed to RESOLVED by Sam (oncall) :white_check_mark:
Marta (support): I'll follow up with affected customers and close tickets after their confirmation.
Ben (product): thanks all. postmortem owners please schedule RCA in next 48h and include runbook updates and automated fallback PRs.
Anika (sre-lead): good work. main risk items: autoscaler backoff behavior, gating that prevented cross-pool fallback, batch job prioritization. We'll track in the incident board. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Sam (oncall): signing off from incident channel, will sync with Anika for the doc.
Priya (ml-runtime): will prototype auto-route-on-throttle this week and open PR.
Jorge (infra): will schedule removal of label gating and add tests.
Marta (support): will push customer status updates in 30m and mark tickets.
Anika (sre-lead): closing thread — keeping monitoring alert for 2h. thanks everyone. :pray:
